newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index sets 10th record close this year.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index sets 10th record close this year.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks powered to their 10th record close so far this year Tuesday as Wall Street took comfort from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks about the economy.
Investors also cast an optimistic eye towards International Business Machines Corp.'s earnings. The computer giant reported earnings that were slightly better than expected after the market closed.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 40.03 points at 6,883.90, beating Monday's high of 6,843.87. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,279 to 1,223 on heavy volume of 571 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow's rise was paced by Boeing Co., which surged 7-5/8 to 114-1/8 and IBM, which gained 2-3/8 to 169-3/8.
The technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index, the Standard & Poor's composite and the NYSE Composite all set new highs.

For much of the session, attention was fixed on Greenspan, who appeared before the Senate to discuss the state of the economy. Although he did warn about the risks of wage-driven inflation, Greenspan's address was upbeat, noting the economy showed vigour with little sign of inflationary tensions.

"Greenspan's speech was much more market-friendly than the comments he's previously made and the comments made recently by some other Fed officials," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
Bonds rallied soon after Greenspan's testimony ended, giving stocks the green light to resume their torrid climb.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose more than half a point, lowering its yield to 6.79 percent from Friday's close of 6.83 percent. The bond market was closed Monday for the Martin Luther King Jr holiday.
IBM's earnings of $2.0 billion, or $3.93 a share, for the fourth quarter beat analysts' estimates by 5 cents a share and compared with year earlier earnings of $1.7 billion, or $3.09 a share.
While analysts viewed the results favourably, many felt an even higher number was needed for IBM to sustain the recent surge in its stock.

"I don't get the feeling we're going to get more exuberance in the price," said Thom Brown, managing director at Rutherford Brown & Catherwood. "But in the long term that's a very good number," he said. "It's an excellent performance."
IBM shares dipped to 168 in after-hours trading, off 1-3/8 from its regular session close.
Far clearer was Wall Street's attitude about Boeing's decision to scrap plans to build a costly stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet.
Industry analysts said the decision removed a cloud of uncertainty over Boeing and estimated the move could save the aerospace giant's more than $2 billion in expenses over the next five years.
In other individual issues, medical ventilator maker Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc. tumbled 5-3/4 to 18 after it reported disappointing results.
Mafco Consolidated Group Inc. jumped 8-1/8 to 35-1/4 on news that its corporate parent Mafco Holdings Inc. offered to buy the 15 percent of Mafco it did not already hold for $38.50 per share in cash.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 12.69 points to 1,376.97, a record.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.02 to 782.72, a record. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.00 to 589.94.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.26 to 411.57, a new high. The average share was up 23 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,567.628 up 52.723 or 0.70 percent.
